policy: Only facts explicitly supported by the cited primary source may be promoted into publishable pathway fields.

records.claim: The Skilled Worker route requires an eligible job, an approved UK employer, a certificate of sponsorship and the applicable minimum salary; the standard minimum salary is currently £41,700 or the occupation going rate, whichever is higher.
records.methodology: Direct review of current GOV.UK Skilled Worker route and salary guidance on 2026-10-11. Confirmed the route requires an eligible job, approved sponsor and Certificate of Sponsorship; the usual baseline is £41,700/year or the occupation going rate, whichever is higher, subject to exceptions and transitional rules.

records.claim: The route normally requires £1,270 in available maintenance funds, held for 28 consecutive days with day 28 within 31 days of application, unless an applicable exemption or employer maintenance certification applies; application fees vary by duration and circumstances, and the immigration health surcharge normally applies.
records.methodology: Direct review of current GOV.UK Skilled Worker cost guidance on 2026-10-11. Confirmed the £1,270 maintenance rule, 28-day holding period, employer certification/exemption cases, variable application fees and usual annual health surcharge.

records.claim: The UK Student route is generally for applicants aged 16 or over with an offer from a licensed student sponsor, sufficient funds for course fees and living costs, and English ability; additional conditions and evidence vary by age and circumstances.
records.methodology: Direct review of current GOV.UK Student visa overview and required-documents guidance on 2026-10-11; age, licensed-sponsor offer, finances, English and under-18 consent conditions were checked.

records.claim: Study permit applicants must demonstrate sufficient funds for tuition, living expenses and transportation; the required living-expense amounts are updated annually and depend on family size and application date.
records.methodology: Direct review of current IRCC financial-support guidance on 2026-10-11. Verified that living-expense amounts differ by application date and family size; for applications on/after 2026-09-01 the listed amount for one person outside Quebec is CAD 23,448, excluding tuition and transportation. Quebec uses separate provincial rules.

records.claim: For points-based skilled visas such as subclasses 189, 190 and 491, an expression of interest is required before invitation; the minimum points threshold is 65, but meeting it does not guarantee an invitation.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Department of Home Affairs SkillSelect guidance on 2026-10-11. Confirmed EOI is required for subclasses 189, 190 and 491 before invitation, minimum threshold is 65 points, and meeting it does not guarantee invitation.

records.claim: Skilled visa processing priorities for covered temporary, provisional and permanent skilled visa applications are governed by Ministerial Directions 121 and 122, which came into effect on 19 September 2026 and replaced Direction 119.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Department of Home Affairs skilled visa processing-priority guidance on 2026-10-11; the official page identifies Ministerial Directions 121 and 122 as effective 19 September 2026 and replacing Direction 119.

records.claim: For visa-required students on academic courses beginning after 1 July 2023, Irish guidance requires immediate access to at least €10,000 for one academic year and evidence of €10,000 for each subsequent year in addition to course fees; courses shorter than eight months use the applicable monthly or capped total threshold. Non-visa-required nationals have separate arrival/registration evidence rules.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Irish Immigration Service Delivery student-finance guidance on 2026-10-11. The official page's last-updated date is 30 June 2025; values and visa-required/non-visa-required distinctions were preserved as published, without inferring a newer threshold.

records.claim: New Zealand implemented final Skilled Migrant Category and work-to-residence changes on 24 August 2026, including changes affecting wage rules and qualification evidence.
records.methodology: Direct review of Immigration New Zealand policy announcement

records.claim: A Finland study residence permit can be granted when an applicant has been accepted by an eligible educational institution and the studies lead to a degree, vocational qualification or qualify as an exchange programme; the applicant must be able to support themselves.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Migri study residence permit guidance

records.claim: Applicants for a first Finland study residence permit need at least EUR 800 per month for living costs; for studies lasting at least one year, the guidance states EUR 9,600 must be available when applying, in addition to tuition funds where applicable.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Migri student income requirement guidance

records.claim: Third-country nationals intending to reside in Luxembourg for salaried activity generally require an authorisation to stay and then a residence permit for salaried workers, subject to the applicable conditions.
records.methodology: Direct review of Luxembourg government immigration guidance

records.claim: Third-country students in Luxembourg may undertake salaried activity subject to the applicable student work limit; after completing qualifying higher education in Luxembourg, a simplified route can apply for salaried or self-employed activity subject to conditions.
records.methodology: Direct review of Luxembourg government student residence guidance

records.claim: Third-country students in Austria may be granted an employment permit for work of up to 20 hours per week without a labour-market test, subject to the required employer application.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Austrian government migration FAQ

records.claim: Eligible third-country graduates of qualifying Austrian higher-education programmes may renew their student residence permit for 12 months to search for employment or start a business, subject to general residence requirements.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Austrian government migration FAQ

records.claim: From 1 June 2026, a Swedish work permit requires salary of at least 90% of the Swedish median salary at the time of application; the current requirement is SEK 34,470 per month based on a median salary of SEK 38,300 published on 16 June 2026.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Swedish Migration Agency salary-requirement guidance on 2026-10-11. Confirmed 90% of median salary for covered first-time work-permit decisions from 1 June 2026; current median SEK 38,300 and threshold SEK 34,470/month for applications received from 16 June 2026. Transitional and exempt categories remain applicable.

records.claim: Sweden's work-permit rules changed from 1 June 2026 and include the new salary threshold and a comprehensive health-insurance requirement; the Swedish Migration Agency also applies employer-condition requirements.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Swedish Migration Agency policy announcement

records.claim: Applicants for a Swedish higher-education study residence permit in 2026 must normally demonstrate at least SEK 10,656 per month for maintenance, with possible reductions where free food or housing is provided.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Swedish Migration Agency higher-education permit guidance on 2026-10-11. Confirmed maintenance requirement of SEK 10,656/month for 2026 applications, possible food/housing reductions, family additions, and related permit conditions.

records.claim: For bachelor's and master's students whose Swedish residence permit was granted on or after 11 June 2026, work is limited to a maximum of 15 hours per week, with specified exceptions for work forming part of education and certain university duties.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Swedish Migration Agency higher-education permit guidance on 2026-10-11; the official page states the 15-hour weekly limit applies to bachelor's/master's permits granted on or after 11 June 2026 and lists exceptions.
